findings.claim: The documented default for `options.allowMethods` now includes `'QUERY'`; if the actual `defaults`/`opts` object in this file still initializes `allowMethods` to `['GET', 'HEAD', 'PUT', 'POST', 'DELETE', 'PATCH']`, the JSDoc is now misleading and will surface a wrong default in editor tooltips and generated docs.
findings.rationale: The hunk only shows the comment, not the implementation, so I cannot verify the runtime default from the diff. Doc/implementation drift on a default value is a plausible issue worth confirming: the corresponding literal in the middleware body (and the Preflight `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header it produces) should be updated in the same change. Moderate confidence — this is likely part of a larger PR that also changes the default, but if the default array was not touched the documentation is simply wrong.

findings.claim: Adding `QUERY` to the default `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` broadens the advertised method set for every existing caller that does not pass `allowMethods` explicitly.
findings.rationale: If the implementation default really changed, preflight responses for all existing users will now advertise the (still-draft) HTTP QUERY method without opt-in. That is a silent behavior change for existing callers and may trip strict security scanners or proxies that reject unknown methods. Low-to-moderate confidence that this matters in practice, but it is worth an explicit note in the changelog/release notes.
